assessments.reasoning: Section 3.8 at pp. 3-5–3-6 gives a single-line form whose execution returns to the following statement and a group form whose lines execute sequentially before the same return. The examples and prose explicitly characterize the invoked portion as a subroutine.

challenge.method: Compared these two forms with the argument-free form, explicit RETURN and the GOTO or IF transfers permitted within a DO subroutine.
challenge.results: The same section describes separate cases for executing the whole program and branching within or outside the group. The exact proposition applies on normal completion of the single line or group and matches both cited passages.

limitations: The finding does not generalize about abnormal completion, branches out of the group, or argument-free DO. The January 1970 printing controls its scope.
